page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7nex.xlarge is a compute-focused instance within the Enhanced family running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at 2.7 GHz, delivering 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading. The platform features 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory configuration. Instruction support includes AVX-512 with VNNI, along with cryptographic extensions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance carries no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistence, and includes a baseline network throughput of 5 Gbps without GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results highlight average single-threaded performance, with stress-ng single-core achieving 1841.49 and Geekbench single-core reaching 1554.0. Compression metrics align with this profile, evidenced by 27.89 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. Because physical compute is restricted to two physical cores, multi-threaded workloads score in the lower percentiles, registering 3867.76 in stress-ng multi-core and 3302.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth settles at 30.43 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput measures 6.35 GB/sec.

The 1:2 compute-to-RAM profile offers qualitative cost efficiency for applications that prioritize dedicated CPU cycles over large memory allocations. The primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of local disk, meaning all file input and output depends entirely on external storage. Given its steady single-thread ratings and 5 Gbps network interface, the instance is appropriate for API services, static web serving, network proxies, light batch transformations, and CI/CD worker nodes.
